exposure: proportion of time in category II fetal heart rate tracing (FHRT) prior to birth
cohort: The study included nonanomalous singletons at term whose fetal heart rate tracing (FHRT) was reviewed by obstetricians blinded to maternal characteristics and neonatal outcomes.
finding: Among term deliveries, the proportion of time spent in Category II fetal heart rate tracing (FHRT) during the last 20 to 120 minutes before birth did not significantly influence composite adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean delivery for nonreassuring FHRT did not significantly differ across groups based on the proportion of time in Category II FHRT.
